confirmed.title: --attach-only is told to compare "every keyed column" against a GET /v1/models response that reports only the model id and max_model_len
confirmed.ticketQuote: .scratch/from-zero/issues/07-model-services.md:100-103 — "4. `--attach-only`: do not start a server; ask `GET /v1/models` on / `http://<serving.host>:<port>/v1`, compare the served model name and every / keyed column against `cfg.models.agent_row`, and refuse to attach on any / difference. `jobs/launch.py` decides when to pass the flag (7.4)."
confirmed.conflictSource: models/table.yaml:9-16 — the keyed `result:` block is `weights, dtype, quantization, max_model_len, served_model_name, env_result, extra_flags`, and experimental_settings/schema.py:603-605 (`_model_row`) makes `cfg.models.agent_row` exactly `{role, family, **result}`; notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4272-4274 — "registry row with a service piece of kind `agent` on this run's row's / `serving.host` whose `service_agent_<replica>.json` claims the same `result:` / block" (7.4 puts the whole-`result:`-block comparison on jobs/launch.py, reading the other run's endpoint file); notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:3892-3894 — "The service asks `GET /v1/models` for the / served model name, compares it and every keyed column against / `cfg.models.agent_row`"
confirmed.detail: vLLM 0.26's `/v1/models` model card carries `id`, `object`, `created`, `owned_by`, `root`, `parent`, `max_model_len` and `permission`. Of the nine members of `cfg.models.agent_row` it can answer only `served_model_name` (as `id`) and `max_model_len`; `role`, `family`, `weights`, `dtype`, `quantization`, `env_result` and `extra_flags` have no observable value on that endpoint, and the attaching process is given no path to the serving run's own `service_agent_<replica>.json` (it knows only host and port, and its `reads:` list at ticket line 19-21 names no other run's directory). The refusal as written therefore cannot be implemented; the only GPU check that exercises it, M-M3 (:443-445), tests a differing `served_model_name` alone, so whatever the implementer picks ships unverified. The ticket does not say which subset the service compares and which the launcher already compared through the endpoint-file `claims`.

verdict.evidence:
TICKET (quoted accurately): .scratch/from-zero/issues/07-model-services.md:100-103 — "4. `--attach-only`: do not start a server; ask `GET /v1/models` on / `http://<serving.host>:<port>/v1`, compare the served model name and every / keyed column against `cfg.models.agent_row`, and refuse to attach on any / difference. `jobs/launch.py` decides when to pass the flag (7.4)."

WHAT agent_row CONTAINS: experimental_settings/schema.py:603-605 — "def _model_row(table: dict, alias: str) -> dict: / row = table[alias] / return {\"role\": row[\"role\"], \"family\": row[\"family\"], **row[\"result\"]}"; models/table.yaml:9-16 gives that `result:` block as `weights, dtype, quantization, max_model_len, served_model_name, env_result, extra_flags` — nine keyed members in all.

WHAT THE ENDPOINT CAN ANSWER: external/vllm-env/lib/python3.12/site-packages/vllm/entrypoints/openai/engine/protocol.py:89-97 — "class ModelCard(OpenAIBaseModel): id: str / object: str = \"model\" / created: int ... / owned_by: str = \"vllm\" / root: str | None = None / parent: str | None = None / max_model_len: int | None = None / permission: list[ModelPermission] ...", and .../openai/models/serving.py:69-73 fills it as "ModelCard( id=base_model.name, max_model_len=max_model_len, root=base_model.model_path, permission=[ModelPermission()] )". So of the nine keyed members only `served_model_name` (as `id`), `max_model_len`, and `weights` indirectly (as `root`, the resolved weights path) have any value on that endpoint; `role`, `family`, `dtype`, `quantization`, `env_result`, `extra_flags` have none.

NO OTHER SOURCE IS OPEN TO THE SERVICE: ticket lines 17-22 list its reads as "models/table.yaml (the serving block only), constants/path_models.yaml, / the run directory's settings.yaml" — no other run's directory; and acceptance A16 (ticket:400-411) asserts the file never imports `jobs.registry`, so the attaching process cannot reach the serving run's `service_agent_<replica>.json` `claims` either. The whole-`result:`-block comparison through that file belongs to the launcher: notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:4272-4274 — "a live registry row with a service piece of kind `agent` on this run's row's / `serving.host` whose `service_agent_<replica>.json` claims the same `result:` / block".

NOT SETTLED ELSEWHERE: .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md has no entry on the attach check (its 7.1 entries are line 29, `--replica`; line 30, the `generation` dict; line 32, the endpoint-file fields; line 34, the live family/weights comparison). The only check that exercises the branch is GPU-only and tests one column: ticket:442-445 — "`M-M3` a second run's service piece started with `--attach-only` ... the same command against a server whose `served_model_name` differs exits / non-zero without attaching."
verdict.correctedStatement: The ticket does not contradict the contracts here — it repeats them verbatim (notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:3892-3894, "The service asks `GET /v1/models` for the / served model name, compares it and every keyed column against / `cfg.models.agent_row`"). The defect is that the clause, as carried into the ticket at lines 100-103, is impossible to execute for six of the nine members of `cfg.models.agent_row`: vLLM's `/v1/models` model card exposes only `id`, `object`, `created`, `owned_by`, `root`, `parent`, `max_model_len` and `permission`, which answers `served_model_name` (`id`), `max_model_len`, and `weights` only indirectly as `root` (the resolved weights path, not the table's alias string such as `gpt-oss-120b`). `role`, `family`, `dtype`, `quantization`, `env_result` and `extra_flags` have no observable value on that endpoint, and the service is given no path to the serving run's `service_agent_<replica>.json` (its `reads:` list names no other run's directory, and A16 forbids importing `jobs/registry.py`). A literal implementation compares an absent card field against a non-null frozen column, differs on every attach, and refuses always — which fails M-M3's "exits 0" case; a sensible implementation silently picks a subset. The ticket does not say which subset the service compares and which `jobs/launch.py` has already compared through the endpoint file's `claims`. The original finding's title understates the observable set by leaving out `root`/`weights`; otherwise it stands.

confirmed.detail: Ticket 08's ordered list puts the first beat at step 2 and the prediction frame's read at step 4, so at the point the ticket calls `emit(0, total, "item")` no value named `total` exists; the only plausible source (`pred_df.height`, or the distinct event count) is two steps later. confirmed.title: F3's `unknown_task` variant trips the completeness gate, never the unknown-task split gate
confirmed.ticketQuote: .scratch/from-zero/issues/09-dataset-builder.md:305-309 — `if VARIANT == "unknown_task":                # a recorded task id in no official list` / `    gone = triples[0][1]` / `    for s in ("train", "dev", "test"):` / `        p = FIX / "splits" / (s + ".txt")` / `        p.write_text("\n".join(l for l in p.read_text().splitlines() if l.strip() != gone))`, and :388 `| `unknown_task` | one recorded task id removed from all three lists | the task id |`
confirmed.conflictSource: data/environments/__init__.py:118-126 (`requested_pairs` re-reads `env.tasks(split)` and takes `ids[:n_tasks]` per split) against the ticket's own steps 3 and 5, .scratch/from-zero/issues/09-dataset-builder.md:38-45 (`triples = requested_pairs(env, cfg.sample.split, ...)` then `done = trajectory_record.done_pairs(sample_dir, pairs)`; raise, naming the missing pairs)
confirmed.detail: Measured against the merged code and the real split files: `env.tasks("train")[:3]` is `['82e2fac_1', '82e2fac_2', '82e2fac_3']`, so `triples[0][1]` is `82e2fac_1` and the fixture writes records for `82e2fac_1, 82e2fac_2, 50e1ac9_1, 50e1ac9_2, 3d9a636_1, 3d9a636_2`. The variant deletes `82e2fac_1` from train.txt, so when the builder runs step 3 it recomputes `requested_pairs` over the edited file and asks for `['82e2fac_2', '82e2fac_3']` on train. `82e2fac_3` has no record file, so step 5's completeness gate raises on the missing pair `('82e2fac_3', 42)` before step 8's split gates ever run. The block exits non-zero and prints a task id, so the check reads as a pass while the gate it exists to exercise (a recorded task id in none of the official lists) is never reached; worse, the id printed is `82e2fac_3`, not the `82e2fac_1` the table implies, so an implementer with correct code may read the mismatch as a defect in their own gate. A variant that only removes a task id from the lists cannot fire this gate at all, because the builder derives the requested pairs from those same lists.

verdict.evidence:
Ticket, fixture variant (quoted with line numbers):
.scratch/from-zero/issues/09-dataset-builder.md:305-309 — `if VARIANT == "unknown_task":                # a recorded task id in no official list` / `    gone = triples[0][1]` / `    for s in ("train", "dev", "test"):` / `        p = FIX / "splits" / (s + ".txt")` / `        p.write_text("\n".join(l for l in p.read_text().splitlines() if l.strip() != gone))`
.scratch/from-zero/issues/09-dataset-builder.md:388 — `| `unknown_task` | one recorded task id removed from all three lists | the task id |`

Ticket's own prescribed order, which makes the completeness gate run first:
:38-40 — `3. `triples = requested_pairs(env, cfg.sample.split, cfg.sample.tasks, cfg.sample.n_tasks, cfg.sample.seeds)`; `pairs = [(t, s) for _split, t, s in triples]``
:45-47 — `5. **Completeness gate** (2.5): `done = trajectory_record.done_pairs(sample_dir, pairs)`; raise, naming the missing pairs, when `done` does not cover `pairs`.`
:55-57 — `8. **Split gates** (2.5): a task id that appears in two splits, and a task id of the records that is in none of the environment's official lists, each stop the build and name the ids.`
:52 — `9. `df = trajectory_record.read_dir(sample_dir, pairs)`` (only the requested pairs are read, so a record whose id was deleted from the lists is never read)

Merged code that re-derives the requested pairs from the edited files:
data/environments/__init__.py:118-126 — `for split in splits:` / `    ids = env.tasks(split)` / ... / `    if n_tasks is not None:` / `        ids = ids[:n_tasks]`
data/environments/appworld.py:212-216 — `def tasks(self, split: str) -> list[str]:` ... `text = Path(self.splits[split]).read_text()` / `return [line for line in text.split("\n") if line]` (re-read from disk on every call; no caching)
constants/path_datasets.yaml:14-17 — the `splits:` block the fixture repoints to `$FIX/splits/*.txt`

Measured (read-only, external/appworld/venv/bin/python):
env.tasks('train')[:4] = ['82e2fac_1', '82e2fac_2', '82e2fac_3', '692c77d_1']; dev[:4] = ['50e1ac9_1', '50e1ac9_2', ...]; test[:4] = ['3d9a636_1', '3d9a636_2', ...]
requested_pairs(env, ['train','dev','test'], None, 2, [42]) = [('train','82e2fac_1',42), ('train','82e2fac_2',42), ('dev','50e1ac9_1',42), ('dev','50e1ac9_2',42), ('test','3d9a636_1',42), ('test','3d9a636_2',42)] — so `triples[0][1]` is `82e2fac_1` and the fixture writes records only for those six pairs. After the variant deletes `82e2fac_1` from train.txt, the builder's step 3 recomputes train `ids[:2]` = ['82e2fac_2', '82e2fac_3'], and `82e2fac_3` has no record.

Neither the errata nor any later ticket line settles it: the only matches for "unknown_task" in .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md, .scratch/from-zero/spec.md and the ticket are ticket lines 305, 364 and 388; the errata does not mention this variant. The in-flight fix listed as a known fact touches experimental_settings/schema.py and data/environments/appworld.py's split_args/build_call quoting and settings inheritance, not `tasks()` or `requested_pairs`, so it does not change this behaviour.
verdict.correctedStatement: Confirmed as stated. One precision: the block does exit non-zero, but the message is step 5's completeness-gate text naming the missing pair ('82e2fac_3', 42), so it satisfies the table's "the task id" requirement at :388 while the split gate at :56 ("a task id of the records that is in none of the environment's official lists") is never reached — and cannot be reached by a variant that only removes an id from the lists, because the builder derives both the requested pairs and the records it reads from those same lists.

refuted.title: report.md's identity line and the row's agent_model/env columns have no source in a build run's frozen settings (`cfg.models` is None)
refuted.evidence:
The finding's premise about the frozen file is true, but its claim that the row/report have "no source" is false: the source is the record frame the ticket already has the implementer read, and it is named in the contracts sections the ticket declares to be its specification.

1. Premise, confirmed: experimental_settings/schema.py:217-220 — `"build": { "sections": ("data", "build", "sample.split", "sample.tasks", "sample.n_tasks", "sample.seeds"), "models": (),` and `"projection": ()` (schema.py:226); `_projection_sections` (schema.py:1176-1187) therefore yields {data, build, sample}, `freeze` (schema.py:1189-1198) writes only those, and `load_frozen` (schema.py:1224-1234) skips a section absent from the doc, leaving the dataclass default `models: Models | None = None` (schema.py:159). So `cfg.models` is None in a build run.

2. But the ticket never sends the implementer to `cfg.models`. It names contracts "1.2 (the example row)" as the specification (09-dataset-builder.md:9-10), and the merged record format carries the field directly: notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:919 `| meta | agent_model | str | the alias from models/table.yaml |`, realized on disk at data/trajectory_record.py:31 `"agent_model": pl.Utf8,` and in REQUIRED at data/trajectory_record.py:88 (`"task_id", "seed", "split", "task_text", "agent_model", "owner_session"`). Contracts 1.2's wording the finding quotes — notes/plans/2026-09-17-contracts.md:1129 `| agent_model | str | the alias that produced the trajectory |` — points at that meta column, not at a settings section; there is no `models` section in a build setting for it to point at.

3. The frame is in hand at the step that needs it: ticket line 09-dataset-builder.md:64 `9. df = trajectory_record.read_dir(sample_dir, pairs)`, and read_dir concatenates whole record files (data/trajectory_record.py:243-252), so the meta columns are columns of `df`. The ticket's own fixture writes the value there — 09-dataset-builder.md:282 `agent_model="gpt_oss_120b", generation="{}", inject=None, commit="deadbeef",`.

4. Nothing in .scratch/from-zero/contract-errata.md (read whole, 147 lines) touches the report identity line or agent_model, so nothing contradicts the above; and no ticket line directs a `cfg.models` read. The conflict the finding reports is an inference about what an implementer might reach for, not a contradiction between the ticket and any file.

One residual fact, not the finding as written: `agent_model` and `env` are absent from data/training_data.py:38-40 `REQUIRED`, and `write` fills any missing SCHEMA column with None (data/training_data.py:42-49), so F2's column-list check (09-dataset-builder.md:346-352) passes whether or not the two columns are filled.

WHY THE "blocks-launch" CONSEQUENCE IS REFUTED:
1. No executor reads the Status of a blocker. The wave script is .claude/skills/ticket-run/wave.js (203 lines): `grep -n "Blocked\|Status\|resolved\|claimed\|blocked" .claude/skills/ticket-run/wave.js` returns zero lines. The script takes an explicit `tickets: [{id, path}, ...]` array (SKILL.md:69) and never consults a ticket's Status or Blocked-by line, so it cannot "refuse or stall".
2. The implementer never sees it either. `grep -n "Blocked\|Status:\|resolved"` over both .scratch/from-zero/prompts/implementer.md and .claude/skills/ticket-run/prompts/implementer.md returns zero lines. A sonnet implementer working only from ticket 07/08/09 cannot produce wrong code, get stuck, or break a hard rule because of an upstream ticket's label.
3. The dispatch set is named by the user, not recomputed. .claude/skills/ticket-run/SKILL.md:35 — "The executable set = the tickets the user named; if the user didn't name any, take every ticket with `Status: ready-for-agent`." 07/08/09 all read "Status: ready-for-agent" (07:3, 08:3, 09:3). SKILL.md:39-40 calls the wave todo "only this session's view", i.e. a bookkeeping aid, not a gate.
4. The item is wave-2 reconciliation bookkeeping that is still open by design, and is covered by known fact (c): a fix round on experimental_settings/schema.py and data/environments/appworld.py is in flight and merges before wave 3 launches, so wave 2's closeout (SKILL.md:108 "`DONE`: change the ticket's `Status:` to `resolved`") has not been written yet. The Blocked-by lines themselves are correct against notes/plans/2026-09-17-construction-plan.md:556-558, as the finding itself concedes.

Under the stated finding definition (ticket contradicts contracts/errata/spec/another wave-3 ticket, names a symbol the merged code spells differently, requires a hard-rule break, or carries an acceptance command that cannot pass), a stale Status label on an already-merged upstream ticket is none of these. It is a main-conversation accounting item, not a wave-3 blocker.

refuted.title: The three wave-3 tickets state the `venv: any` interpreter set differently: 07's A1 adds the system python3, 08 and 09 use the three venvs of the map

.scratch/from-zero/issues/07-model-services.md:267 "SYS=python3", :274 "**A1 — both files import as `any` under four interpreters.**", :275 "for P in \"$SYS\" \"$AW\" \"$PR\" \"$VL\"; do", :279 "Expected: four lines `1 1`, exit 0." — the extra interpreter is really there, but it conflicts with nothing an implementer must obey.

(1) Every errata entry that excludes the system python3 is scoped to a folder whose files need a package that interpreter lacks: contract-errata.md:44 "the `any` import test for `eval/` runs over the three interpreters of `constants/path_datasets.yaml`'s `venvs:` map ... and the system `python3` (3.10, no NumPy) is not in that map and not part of the check (planner: eval)"; contract-errata.md:82 "... not over the system `python3` (3.10, no NumPy), under which every `eval/` file legitimately fails to import because 0.2 gives them NumPy (planner: wrapup)"; contract-errata.md:100 "... which has no Polars (3.10.12, measured 2026-09-17) -> the build keeps 0.1's definition, the interpreters of the `venvs:` map; only `data/probe_input.py`, whose import list is `re`, is additionally checked under system `python3` (planner: data)". Line 100 is the build's own precedent that a stdlib-only file IS additionally checked under system python3, so ticket 07's fourth interpreter follows the errata's pattern instead of contradicting it.

(2) Ticket 07's module-level import lists are stdlib plus PyYAML: 07-model-services.md:15-16 "imports: models/__init__.py (the family through agent(alias), inside the server main), experimental_settings/schema.py (load_frozen)" and :25-27, with transformers/torch/http.server "inside serve()". Run from the repo root: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'.'); import models, experimental_settings.schema as s; print('ok', sys.version.split()[0])"` -> `ok 3.10.12` (system python3 3.10.12, PyYAML 5.4.1, `import numpy` -> ModuleNotFoundError). A1's fourth line therefore prints `1 1` and the loop exits 0.

(3) The reporter states the same conclusion: "This does not break ticket 07's A1 today". An implementer working only from ticket 07 runs A1, sees four `1 1` lines and passes — no wrong code, no stuck implementer, no hard rule broken. What remains is a hypothetical about a future change to the services' module-level imports, which is below the stated bar for a finding.
